title: SPLA/237/2022 of STATE OF UTTARAKHAND Vs ANAND PRAKASH

Hon'ble Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.
Hon'ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Mr. J.S. Virk, Deputy Advocate General for the
State/appellant.
In spite of sufficient service, none appears for
the respondent. It is also borne out from the last
order-sheet while issuing notice on the question of
limitation.
This Court also directed the copy of application
for Leave to Appeal be sent along with the notice.
Since we have already noticed that the respondent on
the question of limitation as well as on the application
for Leave to Appeal. We take the matter on merit.
It is borne out from the record that because of
laches on some part of Government Officials in
giving opinion to file appeal against the acquittal.
In that view of the matter, the Application for
Condonation of Delay is allowed and the delay of 51
days' in preferring the appeal is hereby condoned.
Heard the learned Deputy Advocate General Mr.
J.S. Virk on the Application for Leave to Appeal.
It is borne out from the record that the death of
the deceased was within seven years of marriage. It
was unnatural death and the deceased was subjected
to torture for dowry soon before her death.
In that view of the matter, we are of the opinion
that the appreciation of evidence resorted to by the
learned Additional Sessions Judge appears to be
unreasonable, prima facie.
It is also borne out from paragraph 28 of the
impugned judgment that the learned Additional
Sessions Judge has come to the conclusion that only

when materials are exchanged at the time of marriage
it shall constitute dowry or demand for dowry which
on the face of record, in view of settled principle of
law is erroneous. Any demand for material gains
from the side of the groom, before at the time of
marriage and after marriage are all demand for dowry.
In that view of the matter, we are inclined to
allow the application for Condonation of Delay
finding that there is prima facie, substantial grounds
to allow the application for leave to appeal. SPLA
and IA are allowed. Hence, the appeal is admitted.
Call for the scanned copies (both soft and hard)
of the TCRs. Paper book be prepared and supply the
same to the learned counsel appearing for the parties.
Since the respondent did not appear in spite of
sufficiency of notice, we are inclined to issue bailable
warrant of Rs.25,000/-. The bailable warrant of
Rs.25,000/- to be executed and produced before the
learned Additional Sessions Judge, who shall grant
him bail on execution of bail bond for the aforesaid
amount.
The matter be listed on 17.05.2023 for final
disposal.
(Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.)
15.02.2023
(Grant urgent certified copy of this order, as per Rules) Ravi
